newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/GE active on dividend play.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/GE active on dividend play.

text.p: The heaviest equity options activity on a generally quiet post-Christmas Thursday was in General Electric Co as investors used options to capture the stock's dividend.
GE, up one at 103 on consolidated volume of 1.18 million shares in late trading, goes ex-dividend Friday. The dividend is payable on January 27.
The GE January 40 call traded roughly 16,820 contracts, making it the most active around. The January 60 call traded about 14,265 and the January 40 call traded about 6,400.
Most of the volume in those three options crossed as spreads.
"All the other (GE) options are dead," one trader said.
He said all the volume was from dividend plays and not related to speculation regarding a possible deal between GE and American Express Co.
Rumors of a deal swept through the stock market Thursday morning but a GE spokesman said the company was not interested in American Express.
The busiest American Express option was the January 45 call on the American Stock Exchange. It traded 1,605 contracts.
The January 45 call lost two to 12-3/8 and had open interest through Tuesday of 2,307 contracts.
Also on the American Stock Exchange, the American Express January 50 call traded about 1,000 contracts and the January 60 call traded 1,140.
The stock fell 2-3/4 to 56-7/8. Consolidated volume topped 1.25 million shares in late trade.
In other activity, Motorola Inc options remained active on the American Stock Exchange as the stock extended recent gains.
Motorola was up 2-3/4 at 63-1/8 on consolidated volume of nearly 3.25 million shares.
The stock, which has rallied from around the $54 level, is on track to post its fifth consecutive higher close.
Among the options, investors were focused on the calls, but some put buying was seen, traders said.
The Motorola January 60 call traded 4,385 contracts, making it most active. The January 65 call traded 4,250 and the January 70 call traded about 1,640.
The busiest put was the January 60, which traded nearly 2,200 contracts. The January 55 put traded 1,440.
Also on the American Stock Exchange, a spread in the Merrill Lynch and Co Inc April 80 and 85 calls was seen.
The April 80 traded 1,625 contracts and the April 85 traded about 2,025.
"It looks spread-related," said Robert Rack at Investment Research Institute. "They could be doing any number of things."
He said the firm is bullish on Merrill shares whose options have been largely ignored despite the stock's recent rise. ((G.Crawford, 3124088750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
